At the left end of the spectrum, Politico and Axios centered Zelensky's accusations prominently, leading with his charged language — "smokescreen," "not fair and not honest" — and framing the Ukrainian position sympathetically. A second Axios headline shifted slightly toward a more critical portrayal of Zelensky, noting that "Trump cut deal with Putin after Zelensky ignored his requests," sourced to a U.S. official and introducing accountability framing directed at Kyiv rather than Washington. Toward the center, the Financial Times and wire-style reports from ABC and NBC carried factual, unattributed descriptions: "warns Kyiv," "Russian strikes kill 2," and a hedged diplomatic note about a "new" peace plan. No outlet framed the story with strongly right-coded language. The overall spread is narrow, with the main divergence being whose voice — Zelensky's accusations or a U.S. official's counternarrative — each outlet chose to foreground.
